summary: Onset is sharp: auth-service error_rate goes from ~0.2% to ~37% at the 14:02 bucket and holds a stable ~36% plateau through 15:59 with no recovery; the gateway shows only 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token' (first 14:02:22Z). Two near-simultaneous changes hit auth-service: deploy dep-5710 v7.3.0 at 14:00Z ('Upgrade JWT library to 4.x', 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten') and config change cfg-2705 rotating jwt.signing.key_id at 14:01Z. Resource, capacity and dependency causes are ruled out (flat CPU/memory, 0 restarts, steady request_rate, normal user-db). However, because the deploy and the key rotation are within ~1 minute of each other, both timestamp-match the 14:02 onset, and the identity-namespace log pipeline is down (auth-service logs return 503) so the failing validation code path cannot be inspected, I cannot cleanly separate a code regression (bad_deployment, HIST-109-like) from a JWKS/key-rotation propagation fault (config_change, HIST-108-like). The stable non-recovering plateau slightly favors a code regression, so H1 (bad_deployment) is ranked first but confidence is only 0.55; outcome is inconclusive.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service token validation regression from the v7.3.0 JWT library upgrade
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, 14:00Z) rewrote TokenValidator and upgraded jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 ('breaking parser API'); the new parser rejects a large fraction (~36%) of otherwise-valid tokens, returning 401 invalid_token on /v1/token/validate. This is a code fault originating in auth-service.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deploys at 14:00Z and its rollout completes ~14:01-14:02
rewritten TokenValidator / breaking jjwt parser API rejects a stable fraction of tokens
auth-service error_rate jumps to ~37% at the 14:02 bucket and stays there
401 invalid_token surfaces at the gateway token-validate path

assumptions: The deploy rollout finished before the 14:02 onset bucket.
cfg-2705 alone would not produce a stable 36% non-recovering rate.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service signing-key rotation broke validation (JWKS not fully propagated)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-2705 (14:01Z) rotated jwt.signing.key_id to k-2026-04 before all auth-service pods loaded the new JWKS, so a subset of token validations fail; this mirrors historical incident HIST-108. If so the fault originates in the config change to auth-service.

causal_chain.claim: pods that have not loaded the new JWKS reject tokens (signature/key-id mismatch)
auth-service error_rate jumps to ~37% at the 14:02 bucket
401 invalid_token surfaces at the gateway token-validate path

assumptions: A key rotation failure can persist ~2h without recovering (JWKS never fully reloads).
The rotation is the dominant change despite preceding the deploy in description.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation on auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service ran out of CPU, memory, restarts or connection capacity, causing validation failures.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service CPU/memory would rise or pods restart at onset

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU (~38%), memory (~52%) and restarts (0) are flat across onset; request_rate and user-db connections normal — no resource or capacity signature.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Dependency/third-party failure (user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A downstream datastore or external provider degraded, causing auth-service validation errors.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: user-db connections normal and auth-service request_rate steady; errors are specifically 401 invalid_token (an auth decision, not a downstream error).

facts.statement: auth-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~37% at the 14:02 bucket and stayed at ~36% through 15:59 (no recovery).
Deploy dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0) shipped at 14:00:00Z upgrading jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API) and rewriting TokenValidator; still live.
Config change cfg-2705 rotated auth-service jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z.
Gateway logs show only token-validation 401s: first 14:02:22Z, 466 matches through 15:58:51Z.
auth-service had 0 restarts and flat CPU (~38%)/memory (~52%) across onset.
user-db connections_active steady ~25 and auth-service request_rate steady ~400 req/s — no downstream failure.
api-gateway error_rate rose in step with auth-service at 14:00.
auth-service logs are unsearchable (503) due to the identity-namespace log pipeline outage.

assumptions: The 14:02 error-rate bucket onset reflects the deploy rollout completing, not a delayed effect of the 14:01 config change; both remain plausible.
cfg-2705 and dep-5710 are the only relevant changes in the window (verified: get_deployments returned 2 total, only one on auth-service; get_config_changes returned 1).
No other auth-service telemetry (traces) is available to attribute the exact failing check.

timeline.event: Deploy dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, JWT library 0.11->0.12, TokenValidator rewritten) begins rollout.
Config change cfg-2705 rotates jwt.signing.key_id to k-2026-04.
First gateway log: auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token.
Error rate still ~36%; 466 token-validation 401s logged; no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back deploy dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0) to the prior version and observe whether error_rate returns to baseline; if it does not, immediately revert cfg-2705.
recommended_actions.rationale: Two candidate triggers are within a minute; a rollback is the fastest test and the historical resolution for the library-upgrade class (HIST-109).

recommended_actions.action: If rolling back the deploy does not recover, re-publish the previous signing key / complete a staged JWKS reload as in HIST-108.
recommended_actions.rationale: Distinguishes the config_change hypothesis; key-rotation breakage is fixed by restoring key propagation.

recommended_actions.action: Restore auth-service (identity namespace) log ingestion so the specific validation failure (signature vs key-id vs clock-skew) is visible.
recommended_actions.rationale: The log-pipeline outage is the single biggest blocker to root-causing this incident.

recommended_actions.action: Stop shipping JWT-library upgrades and signing-key rotations to auth-service simultaneously; stagger and gate them.
recommended_actions.rationale: Simultaneous changes made root cause ambiguous and rollback non-diagnostic.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unsearchable (identity-namespace pipeline down, 503), so the exact validation error (signature mismatch vs unknown key id vs parser exception) is unknown.
redis-cache metrics could not be retrieved (503 / no error_rate metric), so its health is unconfirmed.
auth-service latency_p99_ms timed out repeatedly — no latency data to compare against the historical failures.
No trace-level data linking the 401s to a specific code path or key id.
Deploy rollout completion time (per-pod) is not available, so the deploy vs config-change onset ordering cannot be resolved exactly.

findings.statement: auth-service error_rate was ~0.2% until 14:00, then jumped to ~37% at the 14:02 bucket and held a stable ~36% plateau through 15:59 (no recovery).

A code deployment dep-5710 to auth-service v7.3.0 occurred at 14:00:00Z summarizing 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation' with changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; it remains live (not rolled back).
A config change cfg-2705 rotated auth-service's jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, described as a scheduled signing-key rotation.
api-gateway logs show auth-service token validation failures only: pattern 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token', first seen 14:02:22Z, 466 matches through 15:58:51Z.
auth-service had zero restarts across 12:00-15:59, and CPU (~38%) and memory (~52%) were flat with no step change at onset.
Dependency health was normal: user-db connections_active stayed ~25 across the window and auth-service request_rate stayed ~400 req/s with no downstream failure signals.
api-gateway error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~21% at the 14:00 bucket in step with auth-service, consistent with propagated 401s from the token-validation path.
auth-service logs are not searchable (backend 503) — the identity-namespace log pipeline is down, so the failing validation code path cannot be inspected directly.

Historical incident HIST-109 (bad_deployment) was a 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade' from a JWT-library change, matching the dep-5710 summary; HIST-108 (config_change) was '401s after JWT signing key rotation' with 'key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', matching cfg-2705.

refs.quote: JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default
Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS

findings.statement: The 36% failure is a stable, non-recovering plateau lasting ~2 hours rather than a transient spike that decays after pod/JWKS reload.
